visuals.title: Where it is
visuals.text: Swollen lymph nodes in the mesentery near the terminal ileum, so the pain sits in the right iliac fossa.

events.x: Low-grade fever, minimal guarding, still eating

visuals.title: Mesenteric adenitis vs appendicitis
head: Mesenteric adenitis
Appendicitis
rows: Recent viral illness or sore throat

visuals.title: Why it feels like appendicitis
visuals.text: The terminal ileum has rich lymphoid tissue, so its draining nodes in the right lower quadrant swell most, next to a normal appendix.

glossary.Inflammatory markers: Blood tests such as CRP and white cell count that rise when there is inflammation or infection.
glossary.Malaise: A general feeling of being unwell, tired and uncomfortable.
glossary.Generalised abdominal tenderness: Pain on pressing anywhere across the abdomen rather than in one spot.
glossary.Toxic appearance: Looking very unwell, for example pale, sweaty, drowsy or in obvious distress, suggesting serious infection.
glossary.Acute abdomen: Sudden severe abdominal pain that may need urgent surgical assessment.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination rather than from a specific test.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: measures haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: a blood test of kidney function and salts such as sodium and potassium.
glossary.Ultrasound: Imaging using sound waves, with no radiation, so it is preferred in children.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: cross-sectional X-ray imaging of the body.
glossary.Mesenteric thickening: Swelling of the fatty tissue of the mesentery, seen on imaging when it is inflamed.
glossary.Conservative management: Treatment without surgery, relying on rest, monitoring and supportive care.
glossary.Supportive management: Care that eases symptoms, such as pain relief and fluids, while the body recovers by itself.
glossary.Lymphoid tissue: Tissue made of immune cells, such as lymph nodes and Peyer's patches, that responds to infection.
glossary.Hyperplasia: Enlargement of a tissue because its cells multiply.
glossary.Antigen: A molecule from a microbe or foreign substance that the immune system recognises and responds to.
glossary.Lymphatic drainage: The route by which tissue fluid and immune cells flow from an organ to its lymph nodes.
glossary.Perforation: A hole through the wall of an organ, such as a burst appendix.
